title: "naf-shock-patterns"
format: html
editor: visual
---

This post is about the impact of Third Season aka BB2025 on NAF ranked Tabletop tournament play. In particular, we focus on the effect on team popularity. We go beyond the "before / after" changes and look at how the **shock** of a new ruleset, all the roster changes have at on race popularity over time, after the shock in November 2025. In doing so we automatically include a big after shock, the new High Elf roster in march 2026.

I wrote a script that pulls the nightly NAF data dump, and transforms this into a dataset ready for analysis.

```{r}
# # dataprep
library(tidyverse)
source("make_plot.R")
fullrun <- 0

if(fullrun){
  source("dataprep.R")
  saveRDS(df, file = "data/naf_df.rds")
} else{
  df <- readRDS("data/naf_df.rds")
}

df %>%
  group_by(variantid, year, month_date, variantname) %>%
  filter(year > 2024) %>%
  summarise(n_games = n()/2)
```

First let's start with the current state of affairs at time of writing. In 2026, about 5000 NAF ranked games are played each month. September 2026 is the most recent, roughly complete month that we can analyse. As each game has two teams participating, we have about 10000 game-weighted team observations. If all races are roughly equally popular, this translates to 100% / 31 teams = 3% share per race. And about 300 games per team. This is sufficient to compute a relatively stable % share for each team.

# The NAF BB2025 Tournament meta in September 2026

```{r}
mm26 <- df %>%
  filter(variantname == "Blood Bowl 2025" & month_date == as.Date("2026-09-01")) %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  summarise(n_games = n()) %>%
  arrange(-n_games) %>%
  mutate(sort_order = 1:n()) %>%
  select(name, n_games, sort_order)

ggplot(mm26, aes(x = reorder(name, n_games), y = n_games)) +
         geom_point() + expand_limits(y=0) + coord_flip() + ggtitle("# NAF games played by team in September 2026")
```

# Third season: throwing a rock in a pond

We approach the analysis as the effect of a shock over time. Like throwing a rock in a pond. The system is thrown out of equilibrium. It takes time to respond, to adapt to the change. Here we examine the time scales involved. We have seen that monthly game volumes give us sufficient statistics to calculate shares for the 31 races. So let's restrict ourselves to a window of 9 months before the shock, and 9 months after.

```{r message = F , warning = F}
res <- df %>%
  filter(month_date > as.Date("2023-12-31") & month_date < as.Date("2026-10-01") & variantname %in% c("Blood Bowl 2020","Blood Bowl 2025") & gamedate_ok == 1) %>%
  #filter(country == "Netherlands") %>%
  group_by(year, month_date,  name, variantname) %>%
  summarize(n_games = n_distinct(coach_name)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(year, month_date, variantname) %>%
  mutate(total_games = sum(n_games)) %>%
  mutate(share = n_games/total_games)

res <- res %>%
  filter(!(year == 2026 & variantname == "Blood Bowl 2020"))

res <- res %>%
  left_join(mm26 %>% select(name, sort_order), join_by("name"))

res$sort_name <- reorder(res$name, res$sort_order)
```

To "guide the eye" , I fitted a weighted robust second order linear fit through the aggregated data, before and after the introduction of Third season in late 2025.

I present the results by pattern.

Roughly there are six patterns, together with unique stories of three teams.

```{r}
# * Little effect: unshaken
small_eff <- c(7, 9, 20, 21, 22)

#*  instant pos effect with (partial) bounce back
pos_eff_bb <- c(6, 10, 11, 17, 19, 26, 31)

#*  inst drop with (partial) bounce back
neg_eff_bb <- c(14, 16, 18, 23, 25, 28, 30)

#* Instant neg effect without bounce back
inst_eff_no_bb <- c(24, 27, 29)

#* Gradual effect with bounce back
grad_bb <-c(5, 13, 15)

# * Something else 
smth_else <- c(3, 4,  12)

all <- c(1,2,8, small_eff, pos_eff_bb, neg_eff_bb, inst_eff_no_bb, grad_bb, smth_else)
```

First, there are some teams that have a story of their own.

# High elf & Bretonnians: the new roster effect

**High Elf** popularity exploded after the new roster was released in march 2026, and are currently (september 2026) the most popular team together with **Orcs**. **Bretonnians** were newly introduced with the Third season edition, and have a solid popularity at 3-4%.

```{r}
tmp_res <- res %>% filter(share < 0.25 & sort_order %in% c(2) )

tmp_res <- tmp_res %>% 
  mutate(new_roster = if_else(month_date > as.Date("2026-03-01"), 1, 0))

p1 <- make_plot(data = tmp_res, smoothing_group_var = "new_roster", quadratic = T)

tmp_res <- res %>% filter(share < 0.25 & sort_order %in% c(8) )

p2 <- make_plot(data = tmp_res)

library(patchwork)

p1 + p2
```

# Orcs: up and down

**Orcs**, that already were the most popular team in BB2020, became even more popular, surging to an all time high of 10% share of coaches picking Orcs for their tournaments in early 2026. However the observed trend indicates that popularity is dropping again, approach their (still very high) pre-BB2025 levels.

```{r fig.width = 5}
tmp_res <- res %>% filter(share < 0.25 & sort_order %in% 1)

p1 <-  make_plot(data = tmp_res, quadratic = T)

p1
```

# Shaken, but not stirred

There are several races that have virtually not changed at all in popularity.

**Chaos Dwarf** show little effect of the new edition.

- **Black Orcs** and **Goblins** appear unaffected,

- Both **Skaven** and **Lizardmen** transitioned to BB2025 without visible changes in popularity, both showing a slight decreasing trend that was already there before the new edition.

```{r}
tmp_res <- res %>% filter(share < 0.25 & sort_order %in% small_eff)

make_plot(tmp_res, ncol = 3)

```

# Instant drop, no bounce back (Vampire, Amazon, Chaos Renegade)

**Amazons** drop substantially, without sign of recovery. 
As do **Vampires**, dropping from 5% to below 2%. 
**Chaos Renegade** shows an instant and stable drop in popularity.

```{r}
tmp_res <- res %>% filter(share < 0.25 & sort_order %in% inst_eff_no_bb)

tmp_res <- tmp_res %>% 
  filter(month_date > as.Date("2024-06-01")) 

make_plot(tmp_res)
```

# Instant surge with bounce back

Here the patterns show "shock" effects that slowly return to pre-shock levels. 

this pattern is visible for **Wood Elf** , and **Nurgle**.

- **Imperial Nobility** show an initial surge followed by a return to pre-shock levels

- **Old World Alliance** saw a huge increase to 8%, followed by a subsequent decrease, but still remain more popular than in BB2020

- **Tomb Kings** initially increased in popularity, but that effect is fading away in the last few months.

- **Underworld Denizens** show, after an initial clear increase, a slightly higher stable popularity at 2%.

```{r}
tmp_res <- res %>% filter(share < 0.25 & sort_order %in% pos_eff_bb)

tmp_res <- tmp_res %>% 
  filter(month_date > as.Date("2024-06-01")) 

make_plot(tmp_res, quadratic = T)
```

# Instant drop with partial bounce back

- **Slann** managed to survive the transition to BB2025 thanks to the NAF, that introduced a BB2025 compatible roster for them in january 2026. Since then they have climbed back to there old popularity levels at 2%.

- **Dwarfs** show a big drop in popularity, with number of coaches dropping by half.

- **Norse** are less popular as well, but appear to be recovering somewhat, possibly due to improved tiering.

- **Gnomes** took a blow, with stable reduced popularity.

**Elven Union**, **Halfling**

```{r}
tmp_res <- res %>% 
  filter(share < 0.25 & sort_order %in% neg_eff_bb) %>% 
  filter(month_date > as.Date("2024-06-01"))

make_plot(tmp_res, quadratic= T)

```

# Gradual drop with bounce back

```{r}
tmp_res <- res %>% 
  filter(share < 0.25 & sort_order %in% grad_bb) %>% 
  filter(month_date > as.Date("2024-06-01"))

make_plot(tmp_res, quadratic = T)
```

# Initial shock plus a new trend

- **Humans** that in BB2020 were already showing a slow but steady upward trend, became more popular mid 2026.

- **Dark Elves** after initially staying equal, show a slight increase in popularity.

```{r}
tmp_res <- res %>% 
  filter(share < 0.25 & sort_order %in% smth_else) %>% 
  filter(month_date > as.Date("2024-06-01"))

make_plot(tmp_res, quadratic = T)
```

# Predicting the future

Based on the patterns in the data, further increases can be expected for **Slann** and **Pro Elves**.
